title: Kong API Gateway 3.16 adds entitlement enforcement and live operations controls
summary: Kong API Gateway 3.16 adds an OpenMeter-powered Entitlement Enforcement plugin that turns usage records into real-time request controls when credits, limits, or plan entitlements are exhausted. Runtime log-level changes and per-principal plugin configuration also reduce production-operations friction. The release strengthens Kong's monetization and enterprise-governance platform, but largely productizes previously recorded OpenMeter capabilities and provides no evidence yet of adoption or financial contribution, so the score and valuation model are unchanged.
confirmed: Kong released API Gateway 3.16 on September 22, 2026.
The new Entitlement Enforcement plugin, powered by OpenMeter, can block requests in the gateway when a customer's prepaid credits, usage limit, or plan-based entitlement is exhausted.

Administrators can change log verbosity at runtime on Hybrid Data Planes in Konnect and on-premises deployments, with an optional time-to-live that automatically restores the prior level without a restart.
Selected ACL and rate-limiting plugin fields can now vary per request using Common Expression Language expressions based on principal, consumer, and token-claim data.
The release also includes a separately distributed FIPS 140-3-compliant package, overlapping Kong's previously recorded September 3 FIPS announcement.
uncertain: Kong did not disclose customer adoption, pricing, attach rates, bookings, ARR, retention, gross-margin, or free-cash-flow impact for Gateway 3.16 or the Entitlement Enforcement plugin.

The release does not establish that customers will replace external billing or entitlement systems, or that Kong will capture incremental revenue rather than bundle the capability into existing contracts.
Because OpenMeter's acquisition and Konnect Metering & Billing were already recorded, the commercial benefit should not be counted again until usage or revenue evidence appears.
